description:
We are a team of passionate students interested in space, science, and technology. We aim

to identify Earth locations that resemble the environments of the Moon and Mars using

research, data analysis, and innovative ideas. Our skills include programming, web

development, and AI/ML. We are looking for team members interested in astronomy,

geology, GIS, data analysis, and design. We value teamwork, creativity, and collaboration.
summary:
Planetary Analog Finder is an interactive search engine that finds places on Earth resembling a chosen location on the Moon or Mars.

NASA rehearses lunar and Martian missions at analog sites on Earth, but those sites are few, well known, and mostly chosen by appearance. We built a system that turns the Moon, Mars and Earth into one shared global grid described by the same measurable features: terrain relief, slope, roughness, surface temperature, and day-night temperature range. The user clicks any point on a 3D globe of Mars or the Moon, and the system scans Earth and returns the five closest matches. Each result shows a per-dimension similarity score, the measured differences, and a clear “where the analogy breaks” section covering gravity, atmosphere and radiation. A Hidden Gems filter hides famous sites so users can discover new candidates.

It is built on NASA open data: [MODIS, LRO LOLA and Diviner, MGS MOLA; list only what you actually used].

It matters because it makes analog-site selection a repeatable, data-driven search that can reveal overlooked regions, and it makes planetary comparison easy to explore for mission planners, researchers and students.
